sources.entry: Radarr - Automatically download movies via Usenet and BitTorrent (fork of Sonarr). (Source Code) GPL-3.0 C#/Docker

summary.one_liner: Radarr is a movie collection manager that monitors RSS feeds and indexers to grab, sort, rename, and upgrade movies via Usenet and BitTorrent.
summary.what_it_does: Radarr monitors multiple RSS feeds for new movies and interfaces with download clients and indexers to grab, sort, and rename them. It can automatically upgrade existing library files when a better quality format becomes available, such as DVD to Blu-ray. Failed downloads are retried with another release, and manual search lets you pick any release or see why one was not grabbed automatically. It imports downloaded movies, recognizes special editions and hardcoded subs, and handles metadata such as trailers, subtitles, posters, and information for Kodi and others. The README names integrations with SABnzbd, NZBGet, qBittorrent, Deluge, rTorrent, Transmission, uTorrent, Kodi, and Plex. It states that only one version of a given movie is supported per instance, so a 4K and a 1080p copy require separate instances.
use_cases: Automatically download movies from Usenet or BitTorrent
Keep a organized movie library with renamed files
Upgrade existing movie files to better quality releases
Notify or update Kodi or Plex libraries after imports
Manually search indexers for a specific movie release
notable: Forked from Sonarr and aimed at movies rather than TV
Automatic quality upgrades for existing library files
Automatic failed-download handling that tries another release
Integrations with SABnzbd, NZBGet, and many torrent clients
Runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, and Raspberry Pi per the README
caveats: Only one version of a given movie is supported per instance; multiple instances are needed for different versions
GitHub Issues are reserved for bugs and feature requests only, per the README
